newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--European Union leaders sat through the night in Amsterdam to thrash out the details of the new and improved Maastricht treaty. Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis said yesterday he was satisfied with the form the new treaty was taking, given it guaranteed the inviolability of external borders and the right to veto in joint foreign policy.
--Richard Holbrooke, the recently-appointed US presidential emissary on Cyprus, will visit Athens as part of a regional tour at the beginning of August, according to reports.

--Senior judicial officials face disciplinary action following a report by a senior administrative court official which accuses them of irregularities in trying cases involving their junior colleagues.
--Greece sees 1,000-2,000 cases of child abuse every year, a press conference on children's rights was told yesterday. About half of these involve sexual abuse.
--Beaches in the Magnisia region have been plagued by plankton, attributed to a seasonal phenomenon by some and to pollution and pesticides by Greenpeace.
--Albanian underworld elements are using the port of Sarande - just a mile from the holiday island of Corfu - as a base for raids on the island and for the trafficking of narcotics and arms.
--As the first anniversary of the death of late PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou nears, Deputy Foreign Minister George Papandreou remembers his father.
--Judges implicated in a recent inquiry are accused of settling cases involving billions of drachmas in favour of individuals and firms, to the cost of the state.

--Businesses are expected to quickly take advantage of a recent Supreme Court ruling against interest capitalisation by banks and file suit for the return of billions of drachmas. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
